structuralDecisions.decision: Define `FileReader func(path string) ([]byte, error)` in internal/intake/slice.go as the sole filesystem seam CheckSlices depends on; cmd/loom/cmd/intake.go is the only place that constructs a real one (os.ReadFile rooted at the resolved project root).
structuralDecisions.rationale: internal/intake is the use-case layer and must never import os/io/fs directly (architecture-guardrails.md #1, CLAUDE.md's 'every external dependency hides behind an interface'). A function type is the idiomatic Go substitute for a single-method interface here — one capability, no state — and mirrors the existing Check(source, context) style already in check.go, which also never does its own I/O.
tradeOffs: Every call site that needs cross-order slice validation must thread a FileReader through from the CLI layer instead of calling os.ReadFile directly — more ceremony, but it is what keeps internal/intake unit-testable without a real filesystem.
Adds a second seam type to the package alongside Context; acceptable because it has exactly one responsibility and does not entangle with Context's fields.

fitness.property: internal/intake/slice.go and slice_check.go import neither os nor io/fs — the filesystem boundary stays behind FileReader
fitness.verification: golangci-lint depguard rule banning os/io/fs imports in internal/intake, or `go list -deps ./internal/intake | grep -E '^(os|io/fs)$'` returning empty, wired into CI

structuralDecisions.decision: Keep the project-root escape guard (isWithinProjectRoot) purely lexical and run it before readRooted ever calls FileReader, so slice.spec, slice.manifest, and every manifest-listed file path are refused — never read — when they would resolve outside the project root.
structuralDecisions.rationale: slice.spec/slice.manifest arrive in order frontmatter, which may come from an external, lower-trust order (the same Trust distinction order.go already encodes via IsExternal()). A path-traversal attempt must never reach the real file reader, matching the NFR the analyst flagged and architecture-guardrails.md's boundary-validation spirit.

fitness.property: No path that fails isWithinProjectRoot is ever passed to FileReader

structuralDecisions.decision: Keep Slice (order.go) a plain YAML-tagged data struct with no methods; put every cross-order rule in slice_check.go as free functions over []Document, not as methods on Slice or Order.
structuralDecisions.rationale: The unit CheckSlices evaluates — a slice.of group — spans N orders, so no single Order or Slice is the natural receiver for coverage/digest/cycle logic. This matches the package's existing idiom (Check is already a free function, not a method) rather than introducing a new OOP style mid-package.

structuralDecisions.decision: Fold slice-check violations into runIntakeCheck's existing `invalid` counter via checkIntakeSlices's return value, instead of giving the slice check its own independent pass/fail computation.
structuralDecisions.rationale: AC7 requires the exit-code contract (0 only when every order is valid) to stay exactly as it was. One counter feeding summarizeIntakeCheck keeps 'is this run valid' decided in exactly one place, avoiding a Shotgun Surgery risk where two independent validity computations could drift apart under a future change.

fitness.property: The CLI exits non-zero whenever CheckSlices returns at least one violation, and 0 only when every per-order Check and every slice group passes

structuralDecisions.decision: Detect depends-on cycles with a local ~15-line DFS (findCycle) sized to one spec's slice group, not a general-purpose graph library.
structuralDecisions.rationale: The graph here is at most a handful of nodes — one spec's slices. Pulling in a graph dependency for this would be exactly the Premature Generalization anti-pattern design-principles.md's radar flags.

fitness.property: findCycle reports every member of a depends-on cycle, including a self-referencing one, and dangling depends-on entries are reported independently of cycles

structuralDecisions.decision: Do not widen scope.paths to touch shared/DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md in this delivery; accept the Ubiquitous-Language gap for the new Slice/Level domain terms as a tracked follow-up rather than breaking AC10's scope lock.
structuralDecisions.rationale: AC10 makes the scope lock a hard constraint for this run: only internal/intake/**, cmd/loom/cmd/intake*.go, templates/claude-feature-team/intake/**, and this feature's own delivery-record directory may change. shared/DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md sits outside every one of those globs, so adding the terms here would itself be the AC10 violation the analyst flagged — a structural decision cannot override a scope-lock AC. Surfaced to the human in openQuestions rather than resolved unilaterally.

A read failure is reported as a violation immediately, never retried or swallowed.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: Order/Slice domain structs carry no persistence or HTTP logic
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Slice in order.go is a pure YAML-tagged struct; every rule lives in slice.go/slice_check.go as free functions.

antiPatternChecks.notes: Single-process CLI command calling a sibling package in-process; no network call introduced.

Slice/Order hold data with no methods, but this matches the package's existing idiom (Check is itself a free function) and Go's preference for functions over methods on simple data holders — not a smell in this codebase's established style.
slice_check.go is ~390 lines but composed of roughly twenty small, single-purpose, independently testable functions; CheckSlices/checkSliceGroup only compose them.
Exit-code behavior is still decided in exactly one place (summarizeIntakeCheck); slice violations fold into the existing invalid counter rather than adding a second code path.
FileReader exposes exactly one capability (read bytes by project-root-relative path); no caller needs to know whether the implementation is os.ReadFile or a test double.
Cycle detection is a small local DFS sized to one spec's slice group; no plugin/strategy abstraction was introduced for what is still a single code path.
